label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: Choosing a product link made a newsletter signup popup open on top of the page; the checkboxes for agreeing to terms and for news and offers were already ticked, and the close button is only named close modal, so I had to find and press it blindly.
The home page is extremely long, with each product card reading out a huge wall of marketing text before its price, so finding a product by listening is slow and tiring.

element.name: Retailer BK [name] Charger (45W, Smart Display, 180° Foldable)

findings.problem: After pressing Add to Cart the button lost its name and became an unnamed disabled button, with no clear message that the item was added; I only learned it worked by rereading the page and finding the cart panel.

The product says [name]-order now, ship [name] 15th - [name] 25th, which are dates already in the past, so I could not tell whether it was really in stock. Also many buttons and images have no or useless names (This is Product Image repeated 18 times, unnamed quantity and remove buttons in the cart).

The cart panel opened without moving focus into it or announcing a dialog; it has an unnamed disabled button, unnamed plus/minus quantity buttons, and a button named just close, so it is confusing to use with a screen reader.

The checkout page first loaded nearly empty (only a title and empty regions) with no loading announcement, and I had to reread it to find the form; the shipping address field is a combobox named only Address.
